D16·kwqp — 2026-08-05
chose: D15: (a) `sofar statusline --uninstall` — the inverse of --install, deleting the statusLine key so the host tool's own line returns, reporting removed/absent/foreign; (b) `--user` on both verbs, retargeting ~/.claude/settings.json (every project) instead of the repo's; (c) init's statusline hint is suppressed when the personal ~/.claude/settings.json already wires sofar's line. The theirs-wins law now runs in BOTH directions: --uninstall deletes only a byte-for-byte match of sofar's own entry, so it can only undo what sofar did. The settings file survives a removal that empties it to {}. --install with --uninstall is an error, not a precedence rule.
over: Leaving revert to `sofar uninit` (repo-scoped only, so it can never reach the personal settings file, and far too heavy when the user installed nothing but a status line); documenting the hand-edit in the README instead of shipping a command; a --force that removes a foreign statusLine; deleting the settings file when the removal empties it; and letting the hint keep firing on the grounds that it only claims to describe project settings
because: D14 shipped a way to wire the line and no way to unwire it, which is not a neutral omission: it means the only documented exit is hand-editing JSON, and at the --user scope uninit cannot help at all. Symmetry is the fix. The hint change is a correctness bug caught by dogfooding — after wiring the personal settings, every fresh `sofar init` announced "statusline not wired" while sofar's line was visibly rendering, telling the user to fix something that was not broken. Making the probe injectable also closed a real non-hermeticity in the test suite: three init tests had been passing only because no developer had yet wired the line personally, and they failed the moment one did.
